rows.ingredient: block product polynomial -> fast multipoint evaluation -> gcd per block
rows.strongest_antecedent: Pollard-Strassen/Strassen deterministic fast-polynomial factorization skeleton
rows.consequence: The load-bearing extraction skeleton is classical; project notation does not create a new factorization mechanism.

rows.ingredient: m factors per block and m^2 evaluation blocks with m≈N^(1/6), covering m^3 candidates
rows.strongest_antecedent: Balanced Pollard-Strassen/Strassen uses fast polynomial arithmetic at ~N^(1/4) deterministic factoring scale
rows.consequence: PCF5's rectangular m-by-m^2 parameterization is a restricted reparameterization; it is not a speedup and is asymptotically weaker than classical unrestricted factoring bounds.

rows.ingredient: subproduct/remainder-tree fast multipoint evaluation
rows.strongest_antecedent: Standard fast multipoint evaluation by subproduct trees
rows.consequence: The fast-evaluation implementation is standard.

rows.ingredient: batch-gcd-adjacent product/remainder-tree arithmetic
rows.strongest_antecedent: Classical product/remainder-tree batch-gcd and batched small-factor toolkit
rows.consequence: The same-modulus PCF5 cell-gcd list is not literally the many-moduli batch-gcd problem, but its batching machinery is classical.

rows.ingredient: exact cells C_ij={1+i+mj+km^2} partition [m+2,m^3+m+1]
rows.strongest_antecedent: Elementary mixed-radix decomposition of the project table coordinates
rows.consequence: Retain as an exact table-coordinate lemma only; project-local typing is not historical novelty.

rows.ingredient: prime visibility iff p<=U_m=m^3+m+1
rows.strongest_antecedent: Elementary consequence of the project interval partition plus one bounded-multiple argument for p<m+2
rows.consequence: Precise proof: if p>=m+2, p itself lies in the partition interval; if p<m+2, r=p*ceil((m+2)/p) lies in [m+2,U_m]. This is an exact table-interface boundary, not a new factoring principle.

rows.ingredient: fixed-kappa coverage P^+(N)^2<=kappa*N with m^2=O_kappa(N^(1/3)) cells
rows.strongest_antecedent: Classical unrestricted deterministic factoring is already asymptotically stronger than interpreting the support count as an algorithmic complexity claim
rows.consequence: Retain only the exact coverage theorem for this table support; never advertise O_kappa(N^(1/3)) support as a factoring speedup.

rows.ingredient: when a block gcd equals N, refine inside that block by gcd descent
rows.strongest_antecedent: Standard Strassen/Pollard-Strassen block-refinement logic
rows.consequence: The refinement rule is classical.

rows.ingredient: N=2018=2*1009 guard and full-layer Omega(N^(2/3)) universal-visibility obstruction
rows.strongest_antecedent: Project-specific consequence of the frozen table support geometry
rows.consequence: Retain only as a full-layer interface obstruction; it is not a general integer-factorization lower bound.

rows.ingredient: R_H[X]/(fg) product decomposition from comaximality
rows.strongest_antecedent: Ring-theoretic Chinese remainder theorem
rows.consequence: The ambient product decomposition is standard CRT.

rows.ingredient: coefficient CRT for H=pq / product-ring split
rows.strongest_antecedent: Ordinary CRT for the coprime ideals (p),(q)
rows.consequence: The hidden-factor product structure is standard.

rows.ingredient: nontrivial selector idempotent c=(0 mod p,1 mod q) and gcd(c,H) factor extraction
rows.strongest_antecedent: CRT idempotents and standard idempotent/product decomposition
rows.consequence: A nontrivial idempotent already carries factor-equivalent CRT information.

rows.ingredient: h_c=(1-c)f+c g idempotent gluing
rows.strongest_antecedent: Standard gluing in a product ring using complementary idempotents
rows.consequence: The formula is project notation for standard CRT gluing.

rows.ingredient: c=-tr(T), det(T)=1 and converse companion realization
rows.strongest_antecedent: 2x2 characteristic-polynomial trace/determinant identity plus companion-matrix realization
rows.consequence: Trace/determinant readout and converse realization are standard linear algebra.

rows.ingredient: corrected Gaussian/Eisenstein oriented free-rank-2 realization iff nontrivial CRT idempotent
rows.strongest_antecedent: Combination of standard CRT/idempotents with standard rank-2 characteristic-polynomial facts
rows.consequence: The exact grammar-specific equivalence remains a useful project boundary; it is not a general H-dependent no-go theorem.

rows.ingredient: ambient order 12 and fused root counts 4,8,16 at the frozen admissible scope
rows.strongest_antecedent: Cyclicity of finite-field unit groups, elementary cyclotomic root counts, and CRT multiplication of local solution counts
rows.consequence: The root census is standard finite-field/cyclotomic arithmetic expressed in project notation.

rows.ingredient: det(P(T_H))=Res(F,P) mod H for fixed P
rows.strongest_antecedent: Standard companion/multiplication-operator interpretation of polynomial evaluation together with the resultant root-product/determinant identity
rows.consequence: The determinant/resultant identity is standard; no novelty attaches to it.

rows.ingredient: a finite family of fixed H-independent determinant probes cannot universally separate semiprimes
rows.strongest_antecedent: Each fixed probe reduces to one fixed integer resultant
rows.consequence: Precision guard: if a fixed resultant is nonzero, only its finitely many prime divisors can affect vanishing/invertibility; if it is zero, that probe vanishes for every modulus and carries no separating information. Hence a finite fixed family cannot encode arbitrary hidden semiprime splits. This says nothing about H-dependent probes.

rows.ingredient: H=91, c=78 mixed-root pressure witness
rows.strongest_antecedent: Concrete arithmetic regression for the project grammar
rows.consequence: Validation witness only; it carries no novelty authority.

rows.ingredient: N_ONLY_NONTRIVIAL_IDEMPOTENT_OR_EQUIVALENT_SELECTOR_GENERATOR routing label
rows.strongest_antecedent: Standard CRT/idempotent theory for the primitive; project-specific routing semantics for the open generator problem
rows.consequence: Keep only as a project routing label for generating asymmetry from H; do not present idempotents themselves as new mathematics.
